title: RAW: cumulative modulo27 states written by a fixed weighted homophone packet bank
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_FIT. A complete parameterized source-character writer combines IDEA237's differential reading direction with IDEA992's paid modular packet bank. Update s'=s+c-b modulo27, then choose a whole packet whose fixed glyph sum is s'. The reader takes successive packet-residue differences and adds the one global b. Every exact adjacent packet repeat therefore encodes that same source character b; AAA forces bb at its last two positions. No source language, native key, meanings, statistical fit or explained word-shape generation is claimed.

design.scope: One explicitly framed complete source message over lowercase a-z and SPACE, one nonempty output packet per source character, one global alphabet-weight key, one global centering character b, fixed bank and fixed positive spelling weights. No resets inside a message.
design.mechanism: State is the residue of the last emitted packet. Source character c selects the next residue by s'=s+c-b modulo27. The selected state is spelled by a conditionally independent weighted draw from its fixed bank class. Packet shapes and their frequencies are paid apparatus; no free raw-edit transition table is fitted.
design.unit: A complete packet is a finite nonempty string over22 abstract drawings. Physical spaces or layout line breaks separate packets. Source SPACE is a character encoded by its own packet and is not a physical packet gap.
design.contrast: IDEA992 spells each source character's residue directly. This writer spells a cumulative state and decodes differences. IDEA948/1217 instead outputs differences of consecutive decoded source units;995/1327 uses unique word-wheel positions, positive steps and repeat nulls;1301 uses source-word ranks. None is silently repaired or declared successful here.
design.prediction: For every adjacent same packet W,W inside one uninterrupted message, the second packet decodes to global b. Any run of r identical packets forces b^(r-1), not necessarily b^r. Equal-residue but differently spelled packets have the same implication. No distinct-letter conclusion follows from different repeated packet types.

fixed_apparatus.source_alphabet: SPACE=0, a=1,...,z=26. The domain is all finite strings over these27characters, including the empty string and repeated SPACE. Uppercase, punctuation, tabs and source newlines are outside the domain; they are rejected, not silently stripped or normalized.
fixed_apparatus.drawing_alphabet: Exactly22 abstract drawing units. A native realization would require its own justified unit/group binding; EVA working units are not identified graphemes.
fixed_apparatus.weights: One fixed K=(k_g) over Z/27Z, one value per drawing. Values need not be distinct. h_K(w)=sum_g count_g(w)*k_g modulo27.
fixed_apparatus.centering: One b in Z/27Z is shared across the entire declared source scope. It is unknown for a future native hypothesis but never chosen per packet, repeated form, paragraph or page.
fixed_apparatus.initial_state: s0=0 is a public fixed convention at the beginning of every explicitly framed complete message. It is not estimated per message. The external finite-message boundary is part of the input contract; no native paragraph or physical line is automatically such a boundary.
fixed_apparatus.bank: A finite fixed set B of distinct nonempty22-unit strings, with one fixed positive weight q(w) for each member. Every residue must be covered: for each r there is w in B with h_K(w)=r. Bank and q are frozen independently before any key comparison; a candidate key lacking coverage is inadmissible. Gcd alone does not establish finite-bank coverage.
fixed_apparatus.choice: Z_K(r)=sum_{w in B:h_K(w)=r}q(w). At state r, draw w with probability q(w)/Z_K(r), with replacement. Repeated spellings are content-bearing packets, never nulls. Rational q permits an explicit weighted-ticket hand procedure; no randomness cost or bank table is claimed absent.
fixed_apparatus.cost: The full bank, all word spellings, all q weights,22 modular weights, b, the fixed initial-state convention and message framing are apparatus. Directed word formation, whole-word frequencies and historical usability are not explained by the modular accumulator.

writer: Reject a source character outside the fixed27-character domain. Begin the explicitly framed message with s=0.
For each source character c in order, set s=(s+c-b) mod27.
Draw one complete packet from B_s with the fixed normalized weights and write it.
Separate consecutive packets by physical gaps. Layout may wrap only between complete packets; a line break is not a state reset or source character.
Finish after the last source character. No END packet, padding, omitted source spaces or nulls are added. The empty source emits an empty packet stream.
reader: Use the same explicitly framed message boundary, B, K and b. Start s=0.
For each complete packet w, reject it if it is not in B or contains an undeclared unit. Compute r=h_K(w).
Emit c=(r-s+b) mod27 under the fixed SPACE/a-z labeling, then replace s by r.
The writer used r=s_old+c-b, so this inverse returns c exactly at every step. Induction recovers the entire source string, including repeated spaces.

The random spelling choice need not be recovered or regenerated. Different positive-probability outputs may decode to the same exact source; each actual output has a unique source for the fixed apparatus.

For a clipped snippet with unknown incoming state, the first source character is unknown. All later complete adjacent transitions decode from their two packet residues. Do not silently initialize a clipped snippet or every physical line to zero.

likelihood.condition: Fix an independently normalized source law on length-N messages, or explicitly include a source length distribution. Condition on the same known finite-message framing and fixed apparatus. No native source law is supplied here.
likelihood.formula: For observed w1,...,wN, put s_i=h_K(w_i), s_0=0 and c_i=s_i-s_(i-1)+b mod27. P_{K,b}(w1:N)=P_source(c1:N)*product_i[q(w_i)/Z_K(s_i)]. Probability is0 for an unlisted packet or inadmissible apparatus.
likelihood.normalization: At each old state, c -> s+c-b is a bijection on27residues; each chosen state's spelling distribution sums to1. Summing all outputs conditional on any source string gives1, hence a normalized source law gives a normalized channel. The reader formula fixes the only source string compatible with a given output.
likelihood.scope_warning: The Z denominator is the emitted STATE class, not the newly decoded source-character class. A language-only score is still incomplete. The old1335 nuisance profile cannot be copied with source-character counts in place of state-class counts. No unknown-q profiling, native likelihood fit or recovery control is implemented here.
likelihood.symmetry: For fixed K/B/q and a uniform IID source law, changing b merely shifts all decoded character labels and leaves the likelihood unchanged. Thus an exact inverse does not identify b or a language. Other source-law symmetries may likewise preserve competing keys.

source_free_consequences: AA forces source b at the second position; AAA forces bb at the second and third. The first character depends on the preceding state or the explicit initial state.

The same global b applies to ALL exact repeat pairs, even when their packet words differ. Conversely a source b preserves state but may be spelled by a different homophone, so not every source b yields an identical visible pair.
For packets A,B,A, the two decoded inner characters are b+h(B)-h(A) and b+h(A)-h(B); their sum is2b mod27. A closed path of L state transitions has source-character sum L*b mod27.

An exact repeated packet block repeats its internal difference sequence. The first character of the first copy can depend on the external incoming state; do not claim an entire repeated source word without paying this boundary.

Changing one interior packet residue by t changes its decoded character by+t and the following decoded character by-t; all other characters are unchanged. This is an algebraic consequence, not a license to edit or correct a native packet.

Anagrams with identical22-unit multiplicities have equal h_K under every key. Replacing such a packet changes neither adjacent decoded character.1323's key-free anagram orbit argument and its actual capacity stop therefore remain relevant and unchanged.

The native packet count equals source CHARACTER count, not source word count. Physical packet gaps do not mark source word boundaries. Word-frequency invariants for one sourceword per outputword cannot be transferred without changing the contract.
